content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Classification: deviation (fallback target)**

- **Customer exit (11.1 / p0187):** in an eight-year Term, our only convenience right required one year's notice plus a fee equal to a redacted percentage of Estimated Remaining Value (all remaining months at Monthly Base Fee or recent average fees, per p0039), payable 50/50, *plus* uncapped unamortized Conversion costs and Expenses. Both notice length and penalty fail the fallback.
- **Vendor exit (10.2 / p0180):** M&I could withdraw any non-Core Services "at any time" mid-term — a vendor convenience right the fallback confines to term-end; its 90 days' notice already satisfies the notice element (mapped `already_met`).
- **Cure (3 surgical edits):** notice → ninety (90) days; fee → not to exceed three (3) months' Fees; deletion of the add-on cost pass-through that would otherwise defeat the cap; and "at any time" → "effective only at the end of the then-current Term" in 10.2, leaving the 90-day notice words untouched.
- Fallback chosen over preferred because zeroing the fee would force collateral rewrites to 11.2(A) and the 13.5 liquidated-damages acknowledgement. p0181 (regulatory determination) and p0125 (loss of EFT network access) are condition-based, not convenience, so they were noted rather than flagged.
